LocationDescriptions.1:
You stand on a shingle beach at the edge of evening. The sea draws back and comes in again, turning over the stones with a sound like breathing. North, a path climbs the cliff toward a lighthouse. Its lamp is dark again. Someone lit it once, and it burned for a while, and it burned out. East, the ribs of a wrecked ship stick up out of the sand. West, the land goes low and wet into salt marsh. South, an old jetty runs out into the grey.

LocationDescriptions.2: The path zigzags up the cliff face, cut into the rock and worn into a groove by feet. Halfway up there is a flat ledge that looks out over the whole bay. On the cleared ground, one smooth stone sits by itself. It's the start of something, if anyone else comes. The lighthouse is north; the beach is south.
LocationDescriptions.4: At the top of the stair is a round room made of glass. The great lamp sits in the middle, a brass reservoir under a crown of lenses, and it has burned itself dry. Soot streaks the lenses from the last time someone lit it, and the wick is black and stiff. A small wooden box is screwed to the wall beside the stair. The stair goes back down (south).
LocationDescriptions.11: You sit on a narrow bench in a low black boat. The ferryman stands in the stern with a long oar and waits. His hand is still held out, palm up. Behind you the lighthouse is dark. You watched it go out. Ahead there is only open water and the dark. If you have what he's asking for and are ready to go, you can leave. If you aren't ready, the jetty is right there (west).
